What is the $x$-intercept of the parabola shown above?
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the equation of the parabola. From the diagram, we see that the parabola has a vertex at $(-4,1)$ and passes through the point $(0,3).$

The general standard equation of a left- or right-opening parabola with vertex $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
(y-k)^{2}=4p(x-h).
$$

Substituting $(h,k)=(-4,1)$ into the above gives

$$
(y-1)^{2}=4p(x+4).
$$

Now, we need to find $p.$ Since the parabola passes through the point $(0,3),$ we substitute $x=0$ and $y=3$ into the equation and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(3-1)^{2} & =4p(0+4) \\ 4 & =4p(4) \\ p & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-1)^{2} & =x+4.\end{aligned}
$$

When the parabola intersects the $x$-axis, we must have $y=0.$ So, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the parabola and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(0-1)^{2} & =x+4 \\ 1 & =x+4 \\ 1-4 & =x \\ x & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $x$-intercept is $-3.$
